Tara — thanks for the list. Quick answers up front, and I attached a small set of sample artifacts to this message.

- Scan cadence:
  - Weekly authenticated scans for public-facing and critical internal services (credentialed scanner, full agent-assisted crawl for web apps).
  - Monthly full unauthenticated external scans, and quarterly internal host-level vulnerability scans across all envs.
  - On-demand scans triggered by PRs that touch infra or dependencies (CI gating).

- SLA by severity (time-to-remediate):
  - Critical (CVSS >=9 or active exploit): 72 hours to triage + 7 calendar days to remediate or mitigate with documented compensating control.
  - High: 14 calendar days to remediate or scheduled rollback/patch window in next sprint; if not possible, documented exception with compensating controls within 7 days.
  - Medium/Low: tracked in backlog with 90-day target, prioritized by risk.

- Third-party dependencies: we use a dependency tracker (SBOM + Snyk alerts) and create a dependency remediation ticket when a vulnerability is confirmed. Typical windows: for direct dependencies tagged "runtime" we target High in 30 days, Critical matches the Critical SLA above. Transitive or optional deps are assessed case-by-case; tracker links are in the attached csv.

- Representative artifacts attached:
  - redwood-weekly-auth-scan-sample.pdf (sample week report, redacted PII)
  - patch-log-2026Q3.csv (shows patch commit, ticket ID, deploy verification hash)
  - thirdparty-exception-matrix.xlsx (matrix of active exceptions and compensating controls)

Cover note (you can paste this into the binder):
"Redwood Inference maintains a risk-driven vulnerability program: credentialed scans run weekly against production and critical services, complemented by monthly unauthenticated external scans and quarterly internal host scans. Critical findings receive a 72-hour triage response and are remediated within 7 days or mitigated with documented compensating controls. Our evidence bundle includes sample scan reports, patch logs tied to ticket IDs, and an exception matrix documenting compensating controls and owner attestations."

Tara — quick replies below and happy to sign an executive cover note if the auditor needs it.

1) Dependency exceptions: for breaking changes that block a straightforward patch, we require an "exception request" within 7 calendar days of triage with an owner, a compensating control, and a remediation plan and ETA not to exceed 90 days for High severity. Exceptions beyond 90 days require VP-level approval and quarterly attestations. We track exceptions in the attached matrix; each entry has an owner and a review cadence.

2) Credentialed scans: the authenticated weekly scans include package/inventory enumeration on Linux hosts (APT/YUM/RPM + language-specific package manifests) and compare against our SBOM and vulnerability feed to surface missing security updates — results are included in the sample PDF under "Package-level findings".

We will add the two sentences to the cover note and provide the signed one-page attestation if needed.

Best,
Laura Bennett
